newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: BPSM shares rise on H1 results optimism.
newsitem.headline: BPSM shares rise on H1 results optimism.

text.p: Strong prospects for six-month results of Portuguese bank Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor have pushed up its share price, which has surged by more than eight percent in the last two sessions to an all-time high of 2,020 escudos.
But dealers said investors could take profits around the 2,000 escudo level.
"The rise in the share price of BPSM is purely and simply related to the good prospects for its six-month results," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Some dealers said the market was expecting BPSM to post a second half profit of between 8.0 and 8.5 billion escudos. In the first half of 1996, its net profit was 2.825 billion.
One analyst said: "I think that BPSM, like other Portuguese banks, put in a good performance in the first half. I hope to see an improvement in commissions and the margin."
Analysts said BPSM had kept a tight control of its costs.
"The present share price (around 2,000 escudos) is no shock, nor is it cheap," another analyst said.
The prospects for BPSM to exceed 2,000 escudos will depend on its six-month results, dealers said.

"A correction or a rise in the BPSM share price will depend on the profit result. If it is significantly better than expectations, we could see BPSM above 2,000 escudos consistently, but if it comes out in line with expectations or below them, there could be some profit taking," a dealer said.
Share prices of other banks owned by businessman Antonio Champalimaud have risen recently amid optimism over their performance this year.
BPSM and Champalimaud's other banks, BTA and Credito Predial Portugues, present their six-month results on Thursday after the markets close.
BPSM shares stood at 1,985 escudos, up 50, in volume of 375,013 shares at 1100 GMT.
